title: Industry Learning
subtitle: Learning from conversations between Taiwan and Arizona’s industrial communities.
html:
Project overview

At the time, I was studying supply chain management at Arizona State University. I was grateful to hear the Taiwanese delegation and Arizona industry professionals discuss practical issues in semiconductor and supply chain collaboration.

What I learned

The exchange gave me a better sense of what it takes for Taiwanese companies to enter the U.S. market. Alongside products, technology, and capital, companies need to explain what they can offer, build trust over time, and prepare for local operations and service. Hearing people describe their experiences helped me connect classroom concepts with practical questions.

What I learned at the event

I am grateful to the Taiwanese delegation and to Steve Hsu, Executive Director of the Arizona Trade & Investment Office in Taiwan, for helping make it possible for me to hear these experiences in person.

One question stayed with me: how does a company with a good reputation at home tell its story in a way that helps local partners get to know it and consider working with it? It made me pay more attention to how companies communicate, and to the work between the first conversation and providing local service, from finding partners to understanding customers’ operations and preparing post-delivery support.

I also met entrepreneurs and professionals who work in Japanese-language business settings. Their experiences left me with more questions about how Taiwan, the United States, and Japan develop talent, support suppliers, and help companies adapt to local markets.

The event gave me a chance to connect what I learned in class with industry experience. There is still a lot I do not know, and I want to keep learning with humility.
